lines.text: For nine years, Texas was its own country.
In 1836 it won a war against Mexico and declared independence.
lines.say: In eighteen thirty-six it won a war against Mexico, and declared independence.

lines.text: This was a real country. Its own president, its own army, its own money, and embassies in London and Paris.
There was just one problem. It was broke.
lines.say: There was just one problem. It was broke.

lines.text: A hundred and thirty-five thousand people, and ten million dollars of debt it had no way to pay.
And Mexico had never accepted losing. It still called Texas a rebel province.
So Texas asked the United States to take it in.
Washington said no. Texas allowed slavery, and admitting it would tip the balance in Congress.
So Texas started talking to Britain instead. And that changed everything.
Suddenly the answer was yes. In 1845, Texas joined the United States.
lines.say: Suddenly, the answer was yes. In eighteen forty-five, Texas joined the United States.

lines.text: So what if it hadn't? Take a guess.
Today, an independent Texas would be the eighth largest economy on Earth. Bigger than Canada. Bigger than Russia.
It would pump more than forty percent of America's oil, and America would have to buy it.
Thirty-one million people would carry a Texan passport.
But here is the part nobody expects.
Annexing Texas is what started the war with Mexico. And winning that war is how America got California.
No Texas, no war. No war, no California. The whole west coast might never have been American at all.
